title: The Distribution Reward pays on USDS balances held, not on transactions or flows
content:
A.2.2.9.1.1.1 states the purpose: to incentivize Prime Agents and third parties to drive USDS adoption "by providing a financial reward to these actors for **all USDS and sUSDS balances attributable to them**." A.2.2.9.1.2.1.2 sets the rate at 0.2% annualized on those balances, and A.2.2.9.1.2.1.3.2 computes each monthly payment as the average balance over the month times the annual rate divided by twelve.

The choice of base — **stock, not flow** — determines the behaviour it buys. A per-transaction or per-signup reward pays for acquisition events and is maximized by churn: bring a user in, get paid, repeat. Paying on average balance means an Integrator earns only while the deposit actually sits there, so retention and genuine usage are what accrue value.

Using the monthly *average* rather than a snapshot closes the obvious gaming route. A month-end measurement would reward temporary balance inflation on a single day; averaging makes the reward proportional to balance-time, which is the quantity Sky actually cares about.

The design also aligns the Integrator's incentive with Sky's own economics. USDS balances are what generate protocol revenue, so paying a fixed share of balance-time is a revenue share rather than a marketing spend — the reward scales with exactly the thing it is funded by. The rate is a parameter; the base is the design.
description: 0.2% annualized on average monthly USDS and sUSDS balances attributable to a Reward Code, paid monthly — rewarding retained deposits rather than volume or acquisition events.
